these mutants have enhanced catalytic efficiency and specificity for CB1954.

the T41L and N71S mutations enhance the activity of the enzyme for CB1954 by increasing the specificity constant for CB 1954, while the F124K mutation enhances activity by increasing both k(cat) and K(m) for CB1954.

this study has shown that the combination of the mutations N71S and F124K gives a mutant of NTR that shows enhanced catalytic activity and selectivity for the prodrug CB1954 over its substrate nitrofurazzone, and this mutant is therefore likely to give enhanced therapeutic efficacy for virus-directed enzyme prodrug therapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mutations we have studied affect the interactions of the cofactor with the active site and the interactions of the nicotinic acid analogue substrate with the active site.
mutations at positions N71, T41 and F24 can all enhance activity of E. coli NTR towards CB1954, but the combination of mutations at N71 and F124 gives the best overall improvement.
the N71S and F124K mutants are the most promising for further study.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to improve the catalytic efficiency for CB1954 without compromising activity against nitrofurazones.
the catalytic activity of NTR with CB1954 is not simply a reflection of the binding affinity of the substrate to NTR.
it is possible to engineer NTR to improve its efficacy for the CB1954 prodrug substrate without losing activity against other substrates.
